Maya K: We need an SDR one-sheet: short, field-ready, contrasts Redwood inference economics vs cloud-managed endpoints + infra vendors. Hook, 2 bench-safe claims, 3 quick rebuttals, and routing rules. Who can draft?
Jamal: I can. Aim for 150-220 words, plus a 2-line elevator and 3 SDR openers.
Linh: For benchmarks, avoid absolutes. Use a concrete workload and guarded language: e.g. "conversational agent, 2k context, 8 concurrent streams" and phrases like "up to" or "in our tests".
Rahul: Add one small data point about batching+KV cache: "up to 3x token cost reduction vs naive single-request endpoints in our tests" with a link to the benchmark doc.
Sara: Routing: if prospects mention "compliance", "SOC2", "VPC", route to AE-Priv; if they ask about price predictability route to SDR-Pricing; tag with :moneybag:.
Jamal: Draft copy below. Please poke holes.
Jamal: Elevator (2 lines): "Predictable inference economics without sacrificing model quality. Redwood reduces token cost and tail latencies via Dedicated capacity, smart routing, and KV caching."
Jamal: One-sheet (180 words): "When inference cost, latency, and regulatory controls matter, Redwood Inference helps engineering teams ship reliably. Unlike cloud-managed endpoints that autoscale GPUs for bursts and can spike your bill, Redwood provides Dedicated reservations and private deployments that give predictable unit economics and control. Our runtime mixes inference-aware batching, KV/prefix caching, and policy-driven routing to reduce tail latency and lower per-token costs for steady production traffic. For regulated workloads, Private deployments integrate with customer VPCs and KMS for auditability. Field play: open with predictable bill, explain latency SLOs, rebut cloud autoscale with predictable commits + intelligent routing, and close with an easy migration offer. Benchmarks (conversational agent, 2k context, 8 concurrent streams)  in our tests we see up to 3x token cost reduction vs naive single-request endpoints; latency tail improvements vary by model and workload."
Linh: Add legal note: "Benchmarks are representative; results depend on workload and config. See benchmark appendix: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/inference-econ"
Alice: I'll loop in Legal. Keep the "up to 3x" phrasing and include the appendix link.
Rahul: Objection handlers (short):
- "Cloud autoscale is cheaper": "Autoscaling handles bursts but can inflate cost for sustained traffic; Dedicated + batching reduces steady-state unit cost."
- "We already use managed endpoints": "We support managed migrations and hybrid routing so you can start with low-risk fallbacks."
- "We need SOC2/VPC": "Private deployments integrate with your VPC + KMS; we provide audit logs."
Sara: SDR openers: 
- DM: `Hey <first>, curious if you\u0000re tracking inference spend\u2014we helped a team cut token cost by ~2-3x on steady traffic, can I share a brief note?`
- Email subj: `Predictable inference costs for <company>`
- Call opener: `Quick question: do you get surprised by inference invoices when traffic stabilizes?`
